title: Synergy Video Express for Basketball
description: Learn how to install Video Express, film basketball games with the right camera setup, and upload, download and exchange game video. You will be able to get game film to and from Synergy reliably.

modules.title: Installing Video Express
modules.summary: Install Video Express on a PC or Mac and know how it is used to upload game video, box scores and non-game files to Synergy.
learning_objectives: Learners will be able to install Video Express on a PC
Learners will be able to install Video Express on a Mac
Learners will be able to explain what Video Express is used for
Learners will be able to identify who can see non-game uploads
modules.content:
## Installation Links

The Synergy Sports Video Express is a standalone application used to upload game video files and play-by-play/box score charts to the Synergy servers for analysis and logging. In addition to uploading your game film and charts, you can also upload and save non-game files for storage or sharing among your team and staff.

> Note: Non-Game uploads are ONLY visible to your team and/or staff.

Downloading Instructions

Below are two sets of instructions for downloading Video Express. One is for PC users and the other is for Mac users. Please follow the instructions for your device.

### Installation for PC users

1. Click on the link below to go to the Video Express download page:

<https://www.synergysportstech.com/apps/videoexpress/>
![Screenshot: Installation Links](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570453-01.jpg)

2. After you navigate to the Video Express download page, click the **Install** button

3. Open the downloaded file

4. If asked, click **Run**and complete the on-screen prompts

5. After installing, the program will open and prompt you to log in

### Installation for Mac users

1. Click on the link below to download the Video Express app:

<https://www.synergysportstech.com/apps/videoexpress/>

2. Open the downloaded file

3. Click and drag the **Video Express** icon into the Applications folder icon

![Screenshot: Installation Links](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570453-02.gif)

4. Open **Video Express** from your computer's Applications folder, and then log in.

## Accepted Video Formats

### Accepted Video Formats

- .vob
- .mp4
- .avi
- .wmv
- .mov
- .m4v
- .mpg
- .mod
- .mts

questions.question: You are installing Video Express on a Mac and have opened the downloaded file. What do you do next?
options: Click the Install button on the download page
Drag the Video Express icon into the Applications folder
Enter an access code on the login screen
questions.explanation: Mac users drag the Video Express icon into the Applications folder, then open it from there and log in.

questions.question: You are installing Video Express on a PC and the installer asks for permission. What should you do?
options: Click Run and complete the on-screen prompts
Drag the icon into the Applications folder
Skip the prompt and log in on the website
Delete the file and download it again
questions.explanation: On a PC you click Run if asked and complete the prompts; the program then opens and asks you to log in.

questions.question: A coach uploads practice footage as a non-game file. Who can see it?
questions.explanation: Non-game uploads are visible only to your team and/or staff.

modules.title: Filming Games
modules.summary: Set up power, tripod, camera and framing to record basketball games from a high, centered position with consistent backboard framing.
learning_objectives: Learners will be able to set up power safely at the filming position
Learners will be able to position and level the tripod at half-court
Learners will be able to mount the camera and monitor correctly
Learners will be able to adjust the camera angle for correct framing
modules.content:
This guide provides tips on how you should set up the camera, what to frame in the camera's view, and more.

##

## Video Camera Setup Instructions for Recording Basketball Games

Set Up Power to Your Position

- We recommend an extension power cord of 100 feet to avoid having all your gear shut down in the middle of the action because someone tripped on a cord and unplugged it.
- Use gaff tape (not duct tape) to tape the plug to the receptacle on the wall. We also recommend using gaff tape to cover your entire cord run.

Set Up the Tripod

- Position the tripod as close to exactly half-court as you can.
  - This avoids the serious problem of one end of the court appearing farther away and smaller than the closer end
- Do not attempt to zoom in and out during the game
- If possible, prevent people from sitting in the 3 rows directly in front of you
  - Use gaff tape to secure “caution” tape that will prevent people from obstructing your shot.  Try to stay away from an exit row heading down to the floor because people going up and down the stairs will obstruct your view
- Set up the tripod with two legs forward and one leg back
  - This keeps the tripod legs out of your way so that you can get comfortable while shooting.  This also allows you to adjust the camera’s vertical angle by adjusting only the single rear tripod leg.
- If you are not on a flat surface or if there are gaps in the bleachers, secure the tripod legs to the bleachers with gaff tape
  - Bleachers vibrate from people’s movement and tripod legs will shift
- Use the bubble level on the tripod to get the mounting surface level
  - You can do more adjustments after the camera is mounted and turned on using the basketball court as your reference point

Set Up the Camera and Monitor

- Attach the camera to the tripod using the quick mount plate
  - Lock the plate into position so the camera does not fall off the tripod or sit loosely on the tripod head which will cause problems when shooting.
- Plug the camera's power supply cord into the local power
  - Tape the small camera power cord to the leg of the tripod so that it cannot be pulled out of the camera.
- Make sure the camera is using the power supply and not the battery
  - You do not want the camera to turn off in the middle of shooting a game because you run out of battery power
- Use a monitor
  - We recommend the use of an external monitor instead of using the camera’s viewfinder. Plug the monitor’s power supply into the local power.
- Once the camera is attached, lower the two front legs to dip the camera slightly forward to better track the action on the floor
  - You will miss the action on the near sideline at half-court if you do not dip the angle down a bit, but do not worry if you cannot get their feet in the shot when the players cross the half-court line
  - Be careful not to tilt the tripod too far or your basket shots will look tilted and your panning will look odd
  - Do not use the tripod head adjustments to dip the camera forward – it will change the framing of the basket shots
  - You want the camera to track on a slight concave arc and the only way to do this is to lower the front tripod legs slightly

Set Up the Correct Angle

- Framing
  - Make a mental note of where the top of the frame meets the backboard at one end and then make sure the opposite backboard meets the top of your frame in the same place
    - Use the left/right tripod leg height adjustments for this – it is the only way to handle setting up your framing
    - Then use the tripod head adjustments to fine-tune the height of your angle
    - If leg adjustments are done correctly, the head tilt adjusts will not affect the framing as you pan

- Zoom in to obtain the framing shown below
  -
![Screenshot: Camera Instructions for Filming Games](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570456-01.jpg)

- The same amount of backboard should appear at both ends of the court
  - You will notice in this shot that the top of the backboard is barely in view.  In smaller gyms, the very top of the backboard may not be in view.  This is the correct angle.
- By using a 7” monitor, you will become a pro very quickly. Zoom in to obtain the framing shown below

Properly Capturing the Action

- Try to shoot from a position above the crowd.  A platform that sits on the bleachers will help if there is not a higher position like a balcony to use.  Realistically, however, you will normally shoot from the top rows of the typical high school or small college gym.  The ideal position is a high angle at center court.

questions.question: Where should you place the tripod to avoid one end of the court looking farther away and smaller?
options: As close to exactly half-court as possible
At the corner nearest the exit row
questions.explanation: Half-court placement keeps both ends of the court at an equal apparent size.

questions.question: Why should the tripod be set up with two legs forward and one leg back?
options: It lets you zoom in and out during the game
It keeps the legs out of your way and lets you adjust the vertical angle with only the rear leg
It lets the camera run on its battery longer
questions.explanation: The layout keeps the legs clear and makes the single rear leg the vertical angle adjustment.

questions.question: The camera is missing action on the near sideline at half-court. How do you dip the camera forward?
options: Lower the two front tripod legs slightly
Zoom in on the near sideline
Move the tripod to the top row
questions.explanation: Lowering the front legs gives the slight concave tracking arc, while head adjustments would change the basket framing.

questions.question: Which power setup keeps the camera from shutting off mid-game?
options: Run on the battery and carry a spare
Use duct tape to hold the plug in the wall
Rely on the viewfinder instead of a monitor
Plug the camera into local power and make sure it uses the power supply, not the battery
questions.explanation: Using the power supply, with the cord taped to the tripod leg, avoids running out of battery during a game.

questions.question: You have set the top of the frame at one backboard. How do you make the opposite backboard meet the frame at the same place?
options: Zoom in and out while the game is played
Use the left/right tripod leg height adjustments, then fine-tune with the head
Use only the tripod head tilt
Move the camera to the other end of the court
questions.explanation: Leg height adjustments set the framing; head tilt then fine-tunes the height without affecting framing as you pan.

modules.title: Uploading Video, Box Scores and Play-by-Plays
modules.summary: Upload game video, box scores and play-by-plays through Video Express, from starting the upload to monitoring its progress.
learning_objectives: Learners will be able to start an upload from the splash page or Home Screen
Learners will be able to select the season, league, team and game for an upload
Learners will be able to choose the correct file types and video quality
Learners will be able to monitor an upload and handle interruptions
modules.content:
## Instructions for Uploading Files

###

### 1. Initiate an Upload

If you are on the Video Express splash page, select **Start Upload**

![Screenshot: Uploading Videos, Box Scores, & Play-by-Plays](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570457-01.jpg)

If you are on the Home Screen, click **New Upload**

![Screenshot: Uploading Videos, Box Scores, & Play-by-Plays](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570457-02.jpg)

### 2. Choose What Type of File You are Uploading

Choose to upload a **New****Game Upload**, **Box Score/Play by Play,** or **Non-Game Upload.**

![Screenshot: Uploading Videos, Box Scores, & Play-by-Plays](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570457-03.jpg)

###

### 3. Select Game Parameters

Select the **Season**,**League**, and **Team** for the game you wish to upload to. A list of games will appear in reverse chronological order with the most recent game at the top.

![Screenshot: Uploading Videos, Box Scores, & Play-by-Plays](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570457-04.jpg)

###

### 4. Select Game to Upload to

Click on the game you wish to upload to, and then select the **Upload** button in the lower right.

> NOTE: If the game does not appear on the schedule, provide Synergy Support with the following information via email. The game will be added as soon as possible and notification will be sent via email that the game is available for upload:
>
> - Date of game
> - Home Team
> - Away Team

![Screenshot: Uploading Videos, Box Scores, & Play-by-Plays](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570457-05.jpg)

###

### 5. Confirm/Continue

Additional information and instructions will be displayed. You can choose to skip these instructions on subsequent uploads by clicking the **Do not show me this message again** checkbox in the lower left.

Click **Continue** at the lower right of the window to proceed to the next step. Clicking **Cancel** at any time will redirect back to the Video Express Home Screen.

![Screenshot: Uploading Videos, Box Scores, & Play-by-Plays](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570457-06.jpg)

###

###

### 6. Choose Files

A Select Files Dialog box will open. Select the files you wish to upload, and then click **Open** to initiate the upload.

> NOTE: If you are uploading Box Score/Play-by-Play, you will need to upload HTML or HTM files. If you are uploading video, make sure the files being selected are one of the Accepted Video Formats for Uploads (see the “Installing Video Express” lesson).

###

![Screenshot: Uploading Videos, Box Scores, & Play-by-Plays](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570457-07.jpg)

###

###

### 7. Select Quality

If you are uploading a video, you will be prompted to select whether your game is Standard Definition or High Definition. If you do not know, please choose Standard Definition.

###

### 8. Monitor Upload Progress til Complete

You will automatically be redirected back to the Home Screen where the game will be listed in the progress section. Watch the progress from the **Rip**, **Upload,** and **Speed** columns.

##

![Screenshot: Uploading Videos, Box Scores, & Play-by-Plays](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570457-08.jpg)

##

## **Additional Tips**

All uploads are ripped to the local hard drive before being uploaded to the Synergy servers. This allows an upload to be resumed where it left off if it gets interrupted. Any interruption prior to Rip being completed, such as Video Express being closed or the computer turning off, will result in the upload process needing to be started over.

Upload Progress will remain blank until Rip Video Progress is complete. If the upload is interrupted during this phase the upload will automatically continue where it left off upon reopening Video Express. Once upload progress says “Complete” the game is available on Synergy’s servers.

questions.question: You are on the Video Express Home Screen and want to upload a game. What do you click?
questions.explanation: From the Home Screen you click New Upload; Start Upload is on the splash page.

questions.question: The game you want to upload to is not on the schedule. What should you do?
options: Email Synergy Support the date, home team and away team
Upload the video as a non-game file instead
Wait for the game to appear on its own
Choose a different season and league
questions.explanation: Support adds the game and emails you when it is available for upload.

questions.question: You are uploading a box score/play-by-play. Which files do you select?
questions.explanation: Box Score/Play-by-Play uploads require HTML or HTM files.

questions.question: You are uploading video and do not know whether it is Standard or High Definition. What should you choose?
options: Cancel and ask Synergy Support first
questions.explanation: When you are unsure, you should choose Standard Definition.

questions.question: Video Express is closed while an upload is still in the Rip phase. What happens?
options: It resumes where it left off when reopened
It finishes uploading in the background
The upload must be started over
questions.explanation: Interruptions before the Rip completes force the upload to restart; after the rip, it can resume where it left off.

modules.title: Downloading Games
modules.summary: Download Raw or Synergy Full Game video, schedule automatic downloads, and find the downloaded files on your computer.
learning_objectives: Learners will be able to start and monitor a game download
Learners will be able to choose between Synergy Full Game and Raw Video
Learners will be able to schedule a game to download automatically
Learners will be able to locate downloaded video files in the Documents folder
modules.content:
## Downloading Games

We explain how to download Raw, Synergy Full Game, and Synergy Game Asset video via Video Express.

###

### Instructions for Downloading Games

#### 1. Initiate Download

If you are on the Video Express splash page, select **Start Download**

![Screenshot: Downloading Games](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570462-01.jpg)

If you are on the Home Screen, click **New Download**

![Screenshot: Downloading Games](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570462-02.jpg)

#### 2. Select Game Download or Non-Game Download

Choose whether you are doing a game download or a non-game download.

![Screenshot: Downloading Games](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570462-03.jpg)

####

#### 3. Select Parameters

Select the **Season, League**, and **Team** of the game you wish to download. A list of games will appear in descending order.

![Screenshot: Downloading Games](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570462-04.jpg)

####

####

#### 4. Select Game to Download

Click the game you wish to download and then click on the **Download** button.

![Screenshot: Downloading Games](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570462-05.jpg)

####

####

####

#### 5. Select the Download Type

####

You will be presented with options to download the Synergy Full Game or the Raw Video. Click on the type of file that you wish to download.

![Screenshot: Downloading Games](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570462-06.jpg)

#### 6. Select Download Quality

If you selected to download the Synergy Raw Video, you will be prompted to choose between Standard Definition (SD) or High Definition (HD). If you selected to download the Raw Video, you will not see this option.

![Screenshot: Downloading Games](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570462-07.jpg)

#### 7. Monitor Download Progress

After you select the video quality, Video Express will automatically redirect back to the Video Express home screen. A new row for the currently downloading game will be visible.

> Note: If the download is interrupted, it will automatically resume from its stopping point upon reopening Video Express.

![Screenshot: Downloading Games](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570462-08.jpg)

**8. Download Complete**

The download is finished when the Download Progress section displays "Complete." Read How to Access Downloaded Video Files from Video Express (see the “Downloading Games” lesson)to learn where the Raw and Synergy Full Game video files can be located and used on your computer.

![Screenshot: Downloading Games](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570462-09.jpg)

## Scheduling Game Downloads

If you want your computer to automatically download a game once it has been added to Video Express, use this feature to schedule it.

### Instructions for Scheduling Games for Download

#### 1. Initiate Download

If you are on the Video Express splash page, select **Start Download**

![Screenshot: Scheduling Game Downloads](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570463-01.jpg)

If you are on the Home Screen, click **New Download**

![Screenshot: Scheduling Game Downloads](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570463-02.jpg)

#### 2. Select Game Download or Non-Game Download

Choose whether you are doing a game download or a non-game download.

![Screenshot: Scheduling Game Downloads](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570463-03.jpg)

####

#### 3. Select Parameters

Select the **Season, League**, and **Team** of the game you want to schedule for download. A list of games will appear in descending order.

![Screenshot: Scheduling Game Downloads](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570463-04.jpg)

####

####

#### 4. Select Game to Download

Click the game you wish to schedule to download and then click on the **Download** button.

![Screenshot: Scheduling Game Downloads](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570463-05.jpg)

####

####

####

#### 5. Select the Download Type

####

You will have the option to schedule a download of the Synergy Full Game or the Raw Video. Click on the type of file that you wish to download.

![Screenshot: Scheduling Game Downloads](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570463-06.jpg)

#### 6. Select Download Quality

If you selected to download the Synergy Raw Video, you will be prompted to choose between Standard Definition (SD) or High Definition (HD). If you selected to download the Raw Video, you will not see this option.

![Screenshot: Scheduling Game Downloads](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570463-07.jpg)

#### 7. Finish Scheduling the Download

After you select the video quality, Video Express will automatically redirect back to the Video Express home screen. At this point your download has been scheduled, and a new row for the scheduled download will be visible.

> Note: If the scheduled download is interrupted, it will automatically resume from its stopping point upon reopening Video Express. When the game is fully downloaded, the Progress section will say "Complete" in the game row.

this article (see the “Downloading Games” lesson)

![Screenshot: Scheduling Game Downloads](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570463-08.jpg)

## Accessing Downloaded Games

You must have already completed this article (see the “Downloading Games” lesson)How to Download a Game using Video Express (see the “Downloading Games” lesson)to access files on your hard drive.

### **Instructions**

1. Go to your computer’s **Documents** folder
2. Locate and open the **Video Express** folder located in your Documents
3. Locate and open the **Download** folder
4. Locate and open the folder for the downloaded game. The naming structure for all downloaded games is ”yyyy.mm.dd  - Away Team at Home Team.”
5. Open the individual game folder to access the downloaded video files.

You have successfully located the video files that have been downloaded via Video Express. These video files can now be used for editing and burning purposes.

questions.question: You are on the Home Screen and want to download a game. What do you click?
questions.explanation: From the Home Screen you click New Download; Start Download is on the splash page.

questions.question: After you select a game and click Download, what choice are you presented with?
options: Download a box score or a play-by-play
Download the Synergy Full Game or the Raw Video
Download as a PC or Mac file
Choose which team folder to save to
questions.explanation: You choose between the Synergy Full Game and the Raw Video file types.

questions.question: You want your computer to download a game automatically once it has been added to Video Express. Which feature do you use?
questions.explanation: Scheduling lets Video Express download the game automatically once it is added.

questions.question: A download is interrupted when Video Express closes. What happens when you reopen it?
options: It automatically resumes from its stopping point
It is cancelled and removed from the list
questions.explanation: Interrupted downloads resume automatically from where they stopped.

questions.question: How do you know a download is finished?
options: The Rip column shows a speed
questions.explanation: The download is finished when the progress section reads Complete.

questions.question: Where do you find the video files for a game you downloaded?
options: Documents > Video Express > Download > the game's folder
questions.explanation: Downloaded games are saved in a game folder inside the Download folder of Video Express in Documents.

modules.title: Film Exchange
modules.summary: Send Film Exchange invites to opponents and, when you receive one, set up a temporary account to download the film.
learning_objectives: Learners will be able to send a Film Exchange invite from the splash page or Home Page
Learners will be able to choose which games or non-game video to include
Learners will be able to set up a temporary Video Express account from an invite
Learners will be able to download film received through a Film Exchange
modules.content:
## Sending Film Exchange Invites

###

### Instructions for Sending Film Exchange Invites

####

#### 1. Locate Film Exchange button

If you are on the Video Express splash page, select **Send Film Exchange Invite**

**
![Screenshot: Sending Film Exchange Invites](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570465-01.jpg)**

If you are on the Home Page, click on the **Settings** Gear Icon at the top right. Then select **Send Film Exchange Invite**.

![Screenshot: Sending Film Exchange Invites](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570465-02.jpg)

**2. Complete the Opponent Fields**

A new window will appear with fields requesting the Opponent Name and Opponent Email. Fill out both fields with the appropriate information.

- Opponent Name: Name of the person who will be receiving the film exchange request.
- Opponent Email: Email of the person who will be receiving the film exchange request.

![Screenshot: Sending Film Exchange Invites](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570465-03.jpg)

####

####

#### 3. Select Game or Non-Game Video to Send

There are two tabs that allow you to select what type of file you would like to send. You can choose Games or Non-Game Video.

####

![Screenshot: Sending Film Exchange Invites](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570465-04.jpg)

####

####

#### 4. Select Files to Send

Click on the **Include** buttons to select which files you want to send. You can use the **Exclude** buttons to remove a selected file.

![Screenshot: Sending Film Exchange Invites](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570465-05.jpg)

#### 5. Send Invitation

Once you have selected all the files you wish to send, click the **Send**button.

![Screenshot: Sending Film Exchange Invites](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570465-06.jpg)

####

####

#### 6. Confirm

A confirmation dialog box will appear that the Film Exchange invitation was sent. At this point, you have successfully sent the Film Exchange request.

![Screenshot: Sending Film Exchange Invites](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570465-07.jpg)

## Receiving Film Exchange Invites

After you receive a film exchange invite, you will need to set up a temporary Video Express account to download the video. Below are instructions for setting up your account and downloading the film exchange.

[** A full guide to Video Express can be found here.](https://support.synergysports.com/support/solutions/folders/77000329110)

Accessing Video Express

**1. Find your Access Code**

After you are sent a film exchange invite, you will recieve an email with an access code and a link to download Video Express. Make sure you have an access code before you continue.

**2. Download Video Express**

Download Video Express to your computer. You can use the link here: <https://www.synergysportstech.com/apps/videoexpress>

> NOTE: If you need more detailed instructions for downloading Video Express, follow the instructions for Video Express Installation Links (see the “Installing Video Express” lesson) here.

**3. Open Video Express**

After you have downloaded Video Express, open the application. On the login screen, click the link to enter your access code.

![Screenshot: Receiving Film Exchange Invites](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000588365-01.jpg)

**4. Enter your Access Code**

When prompted, enter the access code you received and then click **Continue**.

![Screenshot: Receiving Film Exchange Invites](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000588365-02.jpg)

**5. Set up Account Info**

Fill out your account information. Make sure you enter your email correctly, as you will be sent another link for your password.

![Screenshot: Receiving Film Exchange Invites](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000588365-03.jpg)

**6. Set up Synergy Password**

After you enter your account info in Video Express, you should receive another email from Synergy (this may take a few minutes). Follow the email instructions to set your password.

**7. Log in to Video Express**

Once your password has been set, return to Video Express. Click the login button, and then use your email and your password to log in to the application.

**
![Screenshot: Receiving Film Exchange Invites](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000588365-04.jpg)**

**Downloading Film Exchange**

After you set up your Video Express account, you can access the film that was sent to you. The instructions below will help you download the film.

**1. Start Download**

After you log in to Video Express, select **Start Download** from the splash page.

![Screenshot: Receiving Film Exchange Invites](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000588365-05.jpg)

**2. Start Game Download**

If you received game film, you will select **Start****Game Download**. If you were sent non-game footage (e.g. practice film), then you will select **Start****Non-Game Download**.

![Screenshot: Receiving Film Exchange Invites](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000588365-06.jpg)

**3. Select Game and Download**

At this point, you should see the game that was sent to you. Click on the game and then click the **Download**button.

![Screenshot: Receiving Film Exchange Invites](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000588365-07.jpg)

**4. Download Complete**

**The download is finished when the Download Progress section displays "Complete." To find the file on your computer, follow the folder path:  Documents\Video Express\ Downloads.**

questions.question: You are on the Home Page and want to send a Film Exchange invite. Where do you go?
options: The Settings gear icon at the top right, then Send Film Exchange Invite
Start Download on the splash page
The Include button on the schedule
questions.explanation: On the Home Page the invite option is under the Settings gear icon at the top right.

questions.question: Which information do you enter in the invite window to identify the recipient?
questions.explanation: The window asks for the Opponent Name and Opponent Email of the person receiving the request.

questions.question: You included a file in the invite by mistake. How do you remove it?
options: Click the Exclude button for that file
Click the Include button again on the other tab
questions.explanation: Include selects a file and Exclude removes a selected file.

questions.question: You received a Film Exchange invite email. What do you need before you log in to Video Express?
options: The access code from the email
questions.explanation: The email contains the access code you enter from the login screen link.

questions.question: You entered your account info in Video Express for a Film Exchange. What happens next?
options: Synergy emails you a link to set your password
You must send an invite back
questions.explanation: A second email from Synergy lets you set your password, after which you log in.

questions.question: An opponent sent you practice film. Which option do you select after logging in?
questions.explanation: Non-game footage such as practice film is downloaded with Start Non-Game Download.
